text:
li: Heads-up — seeing a sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate for prod eu-west-1 since ~13:02 UTC. Hit-rate went from ~92% -> ~52% and upstream store QPS spiked. Appears around the time we rolled kernel-selection tweak (commit 8a3f2b2).

ben: any quick graphs?

li: dashboard: https://redwood.infra/perf/cache?range=13:00-13:15 — p95 latency up, token compute time increased. Profiler shows fallback kernels for long-seq paths being picked much more often. Batching heuristics also tightened batch windows — effective batch sizes down ~25%.

priya: that combination would explain higher per-request cost + more backend misses (less effective KV reuse). Do we know which models/routes affected?

li: mostly chat/long-context routes and a small set of enterprise tenants pinned to v2. Kernel selector appears to prefer safety-kernels for sequences >1024 after the change. Not sure why threshold jumped for v2.

ben: infra-bot triggered alert about cache service CPU. infra-bot: "ALERT: cache-service-high-miss-rate [prod-eu] — 13:05 UTC — paging oncall"

oncall: I'm on it. First action: throttle prefetch workers and disable the new kernel policy on a canary pool. If miss-rate drops, we can roll-disable globally.

oncall: Starting canary: prod-gpu-pool-2 -> set feature.flag.kernel_selector_v2 = false.

li: command I ran (canary):
```
curl -X PATCH https://ops.redwood/api/flags/kernel_selector_v2 \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"env": "prod-gpu-pool-2", "value": false}'
```

deploy-bot: deployment started -> rollout kernel_selector_v2=false to prod-gpu-pool-2 (uid: roll/6221).

ben: after canary: cache hit-rate on that pool recovered to ~88% within 3m, backend QPS normalized. Other pools still showing elevated misses.

priya: what's the rollback plan if canary causes regressions? Also want an interim mitigation to reduce stampede risk without full disable — maybe increase prefix-key TTL and enable request coalescing.

oncall: plan: 1) if canary stable for 5m, expand to other pools; 2) simultaneously push a quick prefetch throttle (max inflight per-tenant = 4) and bump prefix TTL from 30s -> 90s for hot prefixes to limit re-warm. 3) Open follow-up to revert kernel-change and add stricter test coverage.

li: opened perf issue: GH#3124 with profiling artifacts and kernel selector trace. Noting kernel selector picks fallback kernels when native kernels report unsupported for kvcache path — looks like a bug in capability detection for v2 models.

infra-bot: action log: "flag.patch kernel_selector_v2 false -> pool prod-gpu-pool-2"; "prefetch.throttle set -> tenant_max_inflight=4"; "prefix.ttl bump -> 90s for hot-prefixes".

priya: Can we capture a small replay set of affected requests and run against both kernel-selection branches? I'd like deterministic repro for CI.

li: yes, saving traces now. Will upload replay set to GH#3124 and run perf job.

oncall: after rollout to all pools (13:12 UTC) the cluster-level miss-rate is back to ~90% hit-rate and token-latency p95 down to baseline. Marking incident as contained.

ben: postmortem TODOs: (a) revert kernel selector commit until we have capability detection fix, (b) add integration tests that simulate kvcache long-prefix sequences, (c) add automated smoke that watches kernel selection churn after deploys, (d) add hysteresis to prefetchers to reduce stampede risk.

li: agreement. I'll draft the postmortem and attach traces/graphs. Quick notes: root cause = capability detection regression in kernel selector -> fallback kernels + smaller batch windows -> lower kv-cache effectiveness -> cache miss storm -> backend overload. Emergency mitigation = feature flag disable + prefetch throttle + TTL bump.

priya: thanks all — great triage. Please put timeline and command logs in GH#3124 and ping when postmortem is up. :thumbsup:
